**Document role:** This guide contains simulator construction, measurements, screenshots, comparison, and simulation limitations. Complete calculations and predictions in the worksheet before using this guide.

# Verification sequence

1. **Calculate first.** Use GUESS for $I=(V_S-V_F)/R$ and $P_R=I^2R$.
2. **Build the circuit.** Add a DC source, switch, fuse if available, $330\ \Omega$ resistor, and red LED in one series path.
3. **Check polarity and values.** Confirm LED orientation, source voltage, resistor value, and an open switch.
4. **Place meters correctly.** Voltmeter probes go across two points. The ammeter becomes part of the series path.
5. **Start the simulation.** Close the switch only after the visual check.
6. **Record values.** Do not replace your hand calculation with simulator readings.
7. **Compare.** Use percent difference for each non-zero quantity.
8. **Explain.** Name a cause of discrepancy and a limitation of the model.

![Protected classroom circuit.](../../schematics/H01_Safety_Lab_Practice_Schematic.pdf){fig-cap="H01 schematic to recreate and verify." width=96%}

# Meter placement check

| Meter | Correct placement | Common unsafe or invalid placement |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Voltmeter | In parallel across the LED or resistor | In series with the load |
| Ammeter | In series after opening the path | Directly across the source |
| Ohmmeter | Across an isolated component with power off | Across an energized component |

# Comparison table

| Quantity | Hand calculation | Tinkercad | Percent difference |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| LED current | | | |
| Resistor voltage | | | |
| LED voltage | | | |

$$\%\text{ difference}=\frac{|\text{simulated}-\text{calculated}|}{|\text{calculated}|}\times100\%$$

# Required explanation

**One discrepancy:** ______________________________________________________

**One simulation limitation:** ____________________________________________

Possible limitations include idealized wires, fixed temperature, simplified LED behaviour, limited source and fuse modelling, and no physical lead or jack hazards.

# Submission

- [ ] GUESS calculation completed before simulation
- [ ] component values visible
- [ ] voltmeter in parallel
- [ ] ammeter in series
- [ ] comparison table complete
- [ ] discrepancy explained
- [ ] simulation limitation stated
- [ ] screenshot or share link included
